items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: we played opposite Kid Ory's band... we all had respect for each other... We got along beautifully.

ctx.x: Right, it was on the northeast corner, and the Suzy Q was on the southwest corner. And right down the street, in the basement, was The Streets of Paris, where we worked with Howard's group.

And later on, they booked us into a place farther east on the Boulevard, called The Jade Room. And it wasn't really a Jazz room. They had different kinds of music going on. But when we worked there, we played opposite Kid Ory's band, and a lot of people thought we might have some conflict, you know, with us with this modern-type band and Kid Ory with his Dixieland band. And it worked out beautifully because we all had respect for each other, you know. They had respect for what we were doing, and we had respect…
